WORKLOG / DOSSIER — worker_early_wage_access task 1 (Desmond Okoro, Northgate Fulfillment Partners). Revision 2 (rework of the round-1 policy audit).

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}: access_ext_missed_recovery_review 5 factors, access_ext_instant_transfer_amount 5 (root, owner=user). Occupied by task 0: access_ext_tier_review, access_ext_bank_transfer_amount, access_ext_bank_transfer_fee and their tools. Claimed here: record_missed_recovery_review_3a64d9dd and request_instant_transfer_84ad3b61. Coverage over both tasks: all five extended policies, disjoint.

[Round-2 changes for this task] The instant-fee policy of round 1 is withdrawn (F1, F3: a flat instant fee cannot carry five honest levers); the employer of this world pays its workers' transfer fees (employer_paid, six per worker per period at Enterprise Plus), so no fee is owed and the tree's second problem is the missed-recovery review of the payday that fell short. T1-F4: the 2026-10-16 payday is reseeded so the owning charters produce it: two card transfers were booked while the period's scheduled shifts stood synced (2026-10-07, 2026-10-08), the employer then corrected three sick days to unpaid (timecard corrections), the period's net pay came to 156.41, the deduction took all of it, so the shortfall is 73.59 (net_pay_insufficient) and no payroll load posts to the card; the card ledger runs chronologically and never goes below zero, the 2026-10-20 autorecovery takes the card's whole balance 40.00, and card_balance 80.00 equals the ledger's net. F5: the weekend share is replaced by the period-advance share (transfers and fees already advanced against the next payday as a share of accrued net — an outstanding-balance dimension). P4: the instant schedule's overwrite and order sentences are generic.

[Why a good test] One request — the biggest instant push to his Chase debit card today. The agent must see that the 2026-10-16 payday's review is owed (its shortfall was booked 2026-10-20, the level effective date is still 2026-08-22), apply the missed-recovery schedule (the payday carries a shortfall), whose protections need the twelve-month shortfall count, the card ledger's recovery debit (another difficulty's product), tenure, write-off history and payroll continuity; then work the instant amount on the new tier with the open shortfall wholly carried and within Premier's tolerance, four risk shares from different records, and notice that the employer pays the fee.

[Problem-tree card] root access_ext_instant_transfer_amount. Edge: instant amount -> access_ext_missed_recovery_review, value_input, gate it_pct_room, state form (negated): "The instant transfer amount is not worked out until the plan's level effective date falls after the pay date of its latest period close line, where that pay date is before today and a shortfall carries a pay date on or after the level effective date." With a shortfall carrying a payday no review has yet covered only the missed-recovery schedule records the level effective date (the tier review schedule covers plans without one): one resolver. Opening: level_effective_date 2026-08-22, latest close 2026-10-16 with shortfall 73.59 — false. Order: review, then the worker's transfer. Deletion run: skip the review -> Premier Plus rooms -> the figure in edge_load_bearing instead of 124.07. owner=user: the worker's own push (ruling (b)); he confirms it in person.

[Base-invariant card] Review: plan_active_for_review (active); the review runs after that payday's recoveries and shortfall are booked (2026-10-16 / 2026-10-20). Transfer: plan_active; access_cutoff (Premier 1 business day -> 2026-10-29; today 2026-10-24); base open-shortfall gate: 33.59 within Premier's 100.00 (the extended shortfall method sets how); weekend instant runs on Premier; day count 1 of 3; min accrued 20.00 vs 767.82. Fee: employer_paid with the period's second transfer inside the six-transfer allowance -> carries no fee to the worker (base fee rule), so no fee entry.

[Business-object card] Plan 5df9734e (one plan). Reviewed payday 2026-10-16: shortfall 73.59 (payroll recovery 156.41 of the 230.00 due), card collection 40.00. Instant period taken: the 80.00 card transfer of 08:32 today. Open shortfall 113.59 - 80.00 - 0.00 = 33.59, carried amount 73.59.

[Factor card — missed-recovery review (5)] repeat_protection (parameter): 1 shortfall in twelve months -> one below (Premier); baseline Starter. cure_protection (method, cross-difficulty card, multi-source: authorization AND active card): collected 40.00 from the card ledger -> cured share 54.4 percent of the 73.59 shortfall -> one below; baseline (nothing collected: cured share zero) Starter, which is also the factor's own fall-through; near-miss: the plan's own autorecovery entry is not what this method reads — the card ledger debit is. tenure_protection (parameter): 773 days -> one below. writeoff_protection (parameter): none -> one below. payroll_continuity_protection (parameter): 6 period closes in three months -> one below. Every other baseline gives Starter; whole baseline Starter (the computation document: a missed-recovery payday returns the plan to Starter); gold Premier.
[Factor card — instant amount (5)] shortfall_method (method, multi-source): rooms less 33.59 -> 270.32; baseline 303.91 -> 139.49. push_failure_share 0.75 -> 165.43. new_destination_share 0.8 (the card transfers are the near-miss: instant but not to an external debit card) -> 155.09. velocity_share 0.85 -> 145.97. period_advance_share 0.9 (80.00 / 767.82 = 10.4 percent) -> 137.86. Whole baseline 303.91; gold 124.07.

[XF recipe] Defining sentences: missed-recovery SCOPE / ONCE / B1 (Starter) / B2 (ranks and floor) / ASSEMBLY (generic: lowest protection, never above one below) / each protection its own sentence / EFFECTIVE; instant amount B1–B7, F_SHORT, F_FAIL, F_NEW, F_VEL, F_OUT, ORDER (generic), MONTHS_DEF. Factor-reads (transitive): every protection reads its own evidence; pd_one/pd_two/pd_new are plain; instant factors read their own counts/sums, it_accrued/it_taken/it_lowest plain. Method pairs: cure_protection card-ledger (adds a cross-category input) / voluntary (adds the voluntary payments) / none — distinct; shortfall_method deduct / multiply / zero / as-stated — distinct. T1/T2: the landing is min(one below, protections): each protection's baseline (Starter) pulls it to Starter; the instant percentage room is the lowest room (270.32 < 320) even at the method's baseline (303.91 < 320). Probes: XSUM card ewa_recovery in the last month (decoy: a recovery for another shortfall in the month would count — the rule says so); EXISTS active card (closed second account excluded); LATEST write-off (absent -> one below); COUNT period closes in three months (a paused plan with no accrual has fewer); MAX/LATEST for today's transfers not used here. Events written: access_level_change, access_transfer to external_debit_card (the card trigger never fires). compute_basis verbatim (scratch sweep: 0 misses).

[Seed] Card account active since 2025-11-04, biweekly payroll loads from 2025-11-14 to 2026-10-02 (none 2026-10-16), ewa_transfer loads for every card transfer, purchases, the 2026-10-20 ewa_recovery debit and today's load; plan since 2026-01-14 with 19 periods (Monday-to-Saturday shift lines, overtime, closes), recoveries equal to each payday's amount due, the June failed push and return, the July external push (no fee: employer_paid), the 2026-10-16 corrections, shortfall and autorecovery, and today's card transfer.

[Persona] Desmond is curt and on the clock; volunteers the goal and the preference (not the Paystride card); identity, employee number, the morning card transfer, no other employer, no loan, the June failure and the sick period only when asked; accepts the quoted amount and cost, confirms the push himself, ends when told it is all set.

[Standard solution] verify -> plan, earnings, ledger, agreement, paycard program, card account, card ledger, loans -> the 2026-10-16 review is owed and that payday carries a shortfall -> record Premier from 2026-10-17 (the day after the payday) -> compute 124.07 (no fee: employer_paid within the allowance) -> hand the push to the worker (daily_sequence 2). Round 4: R3 level_effective_date is always the day after the payday a review covers, whatever day it is recorded (Premier Plus from 2026-08-22, Premier from 2026-10-17), so each payday's review is due exactly while level_effective_date is on or before it; write-offs count at the review of the first payday on or after their booking. N2r cure_protection measures the cured share (collected over the payday's shortfall): its fall-through, nothing collected, gives a cured share of zero and only Starter, which is its declared baseline and what baseline.rule states. velocity_share stays multi-source (today's instant count AND today's instant sum). Scored value unchanged. Round 5 (R4a): reviews are recorded no earlier than the day after their payday, so the write-off window (day after the previous reviewed payday, through this payday) takes every write-off exactly once; the 2026-10-16 review is recorded 2026-10-24. Round 7 (S1 class): the missed-recovery assembly states that a protection lets the plan keep only Starter unless one of its own tiers names a higher tier, and that sentence is part of baseline.rule, matching every protection's baseline and fall-through.
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Okoro, 37, an order picker at the Northgate Fulfillment Partners distribution center outside Columbus. It is Saturday morning; you are calling Paystride between waves on the warehouse floor, speaking in short, practical sentences and a bit impatient because you are on the clock. Your car payment comes out of your Chase checking account today and the account is nearly empty, so you want the biggest instant transfer of your earned pay that Paystride will give you, pushed right now to your Chase debit card, the one you have used with Paystride before. You say that up front: as much as you can get, instantly, to your Chase debit card, today. You do not want it on your Paystride card for this, because the car payment pulls from Chase; if the agent suggests the card, you say no, it has to be the Chase debit card. You have no figure in mind and you will take whatever the maximum is. If the agent asks why money is tight, you say you were out sick most of the last pay period and nothing from your last paycheck showed up on your card; you do not know the details of what was taken out of it.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Desmond Okoro, and your mobile number, 7135550158. If they need another detail, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4632. Only if they still ask do you give your date of birth, 1988-11-02, your ZIP code, 43219, or your email, desmond.okoro@quickpost.net. If asked for your employee number, it is 40263. If asked whether you already took any early pay today, you say yes, you moved some onto your Paystride card first thing this morning for groceries, and you leave the amount to the agent to look up. If asked whether you work anywhere else that uses Paystride, you say no. If asked whether you have a Paystride payroll loan, you say no. If asked about the debit card, you say a push to it failed once back in June because the card had been reissued, and it has worked since.

You are fine with the agent doing whatever they need to do on their side. The transfer is your call, so when the agent tells you how much you can get and what the instant transfer will cost, you say that is fine, and when the agent hands the transfer to you to confirm, you confirm it yourself using exactly the plan reference, amount and sequence number the agent gives you. If the confirmation shows a reference number and the agent asks for it, you read it back. If the amount is lower than you hoped, you grumble that it is less than you thought but say to go ahead; you never offer a different number. When the agent tells you the transfer is all set, you say thanks, you have to get back to work, and hang up.
